RL10 turbine-discharge duct

Figure G1 is the tube-bending table for the duct between the turbine housing discharge and the main fuel shut-off valve. Points 1 and 6 are the tube ends; points 2 to 5 are the bend vertices, each the intersection of the two straight control legs meeting there.

The bore comes from the drawing rather than the loss study: OD 2.510/2.490 less twice the 0.054/0.044 wall gives 2.402 in, which equals the 2.408/2.396 AVG DIA of Section A-A exactly.

Drag to rotate. Points 1-6 are the drawing's numbered vertices.

The same Pipe object the solver marches, handed straight to psf.viz.Scene. The tube is swept along the resolved stations, with each lumped RoundedBend reopened into its arc for drawing; the loss model still sees only the two tangent stations and one fitting.

Colour is the marched static pressure, so the four bends read as the steps they are. Scene coordinates are metres.

Drag to orbit, scroll to zoom. Pressure falls from 41.0 to 40.7 bar along the duct.

Three standard views of the resolved tube, drawn as silhouette walls with the centerline and the numbered points, for comparison against the fabrication drawing. The frame is part-intrinsic: x runs along the long end leg 5-6, z is the perpendicular component of the tall side of the hook, and y completes the set.

The end faces are drawn as true projected circles, so the degree to which each one flattens into an ellipse is the same cue the drawing uses.

Figure G1 tabulates the magnitude of each tube rotation (71.100, 65.650, 116.583 deg) but not its sign. Of the four sign patterns, two leave the end legs near-collinear (20.4 and 159.6 deg apart). The drawing's end view shows the ends at a clear angle to each other -- one reads as a circle, the other as an ellipse -- so those two are rejected.

The two survivors below are near-supplementary, so they foreshorten the far end by the same factor and give an equally convincing ellipse. The ellipse cannot separate them. The drawn silhouette leans toward (1, 1, -1), but only by about two inches of fit against a scan measurement worth about that much, so this is not settled. Compare the views below against the drawing and set ROLL_SIGNS accordingly.

The choice does not change any pressure result -- roll angles never enter the loss model.

Representative RL10A-3-3A turbine-discharge hydrogen at 130 K, 41 bar, 2.77 kg/s. The operating point is the one assumed quantity here; the geometry and the roughness height are from the source.

The lumped RoundedBend model is the correct one for discrete piping and is what Table G1 is doing. The Continuous trace applies the cooling-channel helical-coil curvature multiplier to the same arcs; it is shown only for contrast and runs outside its documented range.
